newsitem.title: USA: Grace unlocks value with spinoff.
newsitem.headline: Grace unlocks value with spinoff.

text.p: W.R. Grace completed the major part of its restructuring program which has lasted more than two years under chief executive Albert Costello with a deal which will generate significant benefit for shareholders.

On Thursday, Boca Raton, Fla-based Grace said it would merge its packaging business with New Jersey-based Sealed Air Corp to create the world's largest specialty packaging company with a market capitalisation of $5.0 billion.
"This is a deal made in heaven. We can add four to six points to the price earnings ratio on which our packaging business is trading," Costello said in a telephone interview.
Analysts agreed, noting the packaging business, which accounts for 75 percent of revenues, had not been properly valued by investors.

"In the past, the Street has been paying a (price earnings) multiple of 15 for the packaging business while the competition has been on 21 times. Grace management has rerated the business to the top rank," said Jaine Mehring, analyst at Smith Barney.

Grace has managed a transaction that will be tax free to its shareholders under which they will receive $1.8 billion of convertible preference shares plus $1.9 billion in a new company to be formed by the merger of its packaging division with Sealed Air.
The new company, to be based in Saddle Brook, NJ, will be 63 percent owned by Grace shareholders and 37 percent by Sealed Air holders and will have sales of $2.5 billion.
Its main business is the Cryovac brand of food packaging.

As part of the spinoff, the rest of Grace's business, its specialty and construction chemicals will become a separate company and will receive $1.2 billion in cash, which it will use to pay down debt.
Grace Specialty Chemicals Co will then be in the market for acquisitions in the range of $200-$300 million, Costello said.
"There are some attractive businesses out there, mostly international," Costello said.
Smith Barney's Mehring said that the chemicals business should benefit from an upturn in its major market, manufacturing catalysts for oil refineries.
"We see real growth potential, this company will have a market capitalisation of $2.0-$2.5 billion," said Costello, who will head the new company.
He said that investors were pleased that the company had been able to achieve tax-free status for its shareholders under the trms of the so-called "Morris Trust", a provision that permits such deals.
Although there are moves afoot to kill the provision, Costello said that he had been advised by two leading law firms that the deal met the terms of the provision.
"People are very pleased that we managed to meet the terms," he said.
Mehring said that she believed the key to the deal was not the paying down of debt or the tax free status.
"It is nice, it is the icing on the cake, but the key is the creation of value," she said.
Mehring has had Grace, whose stock closed up 1-3/4 at 68-1/4, as a "strong buy". ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
